title: Prompt-injected agent fills control-plane host disk with per-approval screenshot PNGs that are never reclaimed (no pending-approval cap)
description: On a desktop-template sandbox, every agent tool call whose policy decision is REQUIRE_APPROVAL causes the control plane to (a) create a pending approval row with no per-sandbox cap and (b) take a full-screen screenshot and write it to settings.home/captures/{aid}.png. No code path removes these PNG files on approval decision, expiry, or sandbox deletion, and nothing caps the number of concurrently pending approvals. A lowest-trust agent (the assumed prompt-injected principal) can therefore issue an unbounded series of cheap gated calls (e.g. delete_file, or any non-allowlisted exec), each costing one host-disk screenshot that is retained forever, growing settings.home without bound and surviving even sandbox deletion.
root_cause: AgentBox._call_tool writes captures/{aid}.png at service.py:325 for every REQUIRE_APPROVAL on a desktop template, but neither decide() (service.py:384-422), expire_stale() (service.py:371-382), nor SandboxManager.delete() (sandbox.py:443-455) ever deletes the capture file; ApprovalStore.create (approvals.py:49-59) also enforces no per-sandbox or aggregate pending count. The only cost gate is tool_concurrency (serial 202 responses evade it) and the snapshot_quota gate (only reached on ALLOW decisions, not on REQUIRE_APPROVAL).
intended_behavior: Agent-driven approval work must be bounded: a per-sandbox pending-approval cap should reject further gated calls past a limit, and the request-time capture PNG must be reclaimed when the approval reaches a terminal state (decided/expired) and when the sandbox is deleted, so one low-trust principal cannot persistently grow shared host disk.

trace.description: Agent tool call (POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/{tool}) enters tool handling; tool is attacker-chosen.
policy.decide returns REQUIRE_APPROVAL for cheap gated tools (delete_file, non-allowlisted exec per default_policy.yaml).
On a desktop template (_capture: template_of(sid).desktop) a full-screen screenshot PNG is taken; screenshot bytes are read uncapped (sandbox.py:714-722).
Inserts a pending approval with no per-sandbox / aggregate count check — unbounded pending approvals.
Per-approval PNG written to settings.home/captures; no code removes it on deny/expire (service.py decide/expire_stale) or sandbox delete (sandbox.py:443-455).

evidence.description: The sole writer of captures/{aid}.png; executed once per REQUIRE_APPROVAL on a desktop template.
create() has no per-sandbox or aggregate pending-approval cap.
expire_stale marks approvals EXPIRED but never deletes the approval row or its capture PNG.
decide (deny/execute branches) finalize the approval status but never delete the capture PNG.
SandboxManager.delete removes container + snapshot images only; never touches settings.home/captures.
(sandbox.py) screenshot reads the full desktop PNG with no size cap, so each retained capture can be large.

conditions.description: Attacker holds an agent token (agt_) for one desktop-template sandbox — the lowest-trust, prompt-injection-assumed principal.
Sandbox uses a desktop template (template_of(sid).desktop True) and captures is configured (settings.home/captures, the default in api.py:75).
Sustained but cheap: one gated tool call per retained PNG; files persist across approval decisions, expiry, and sandbox deletion.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent token confined to its own desktop-template sandbox wants to degrade the shared control plane by exhausting host disk under settings.home.
instructions: Repeatedly issue a gated tool call that maps to REQUIRE_APPROVAL in default_policy.yaml (delete_file, or any exec outside the read-only allowlist). Each returns 202 pending.
Each call creates a pending approval (no cap) and writes settings.home/captures/{approval_id}.png (full-screen screenshot).
Let the approvals be denied or simply expire after approval_timeout; delete the sandbox. Observe captures/*.png files remain.
Local reproduction: /tmp/.../sbx5 h-queue /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h.py drives the real AgentBox._call_tool / decide / expire_stale with a real ApprovalStore and a stubbed desktop screenshot.
execution.observed_result: pending_approvals_created: 30 (no per-sandbox cap); png_files_on_disk: 30; after denying 1 and expiring 29, png_files_after_deny_and_expire: 30 — every capture PNG persisted. captures_dir_bytes grew linearly with request count and is never reclaimed; SandboxManager.delete (source) does not touch captures.

remediation.strategy: Bound and reclaim approval artifacts: (1) enforce a per-sandbox pending-approval cap in _call_tool/ApprovalStore before creating a new approval (return 429 past the limit); (2) delete captures/{aid}.png whenever an approval reaches a terminal state (finish()/claim() to EXPIRED/DENIED/EXECUTED/FAILED) and when the sandbox is deleted; (3) optionally cap total captures bytes and prune oldest.

code_changes.fixed_code:
# In SandboxManager.delete(sid), after status->deleted, have the service also remove
# all captures for approvals belonging to sid (iterate approvals.list(sandbox_id=sid) and unlink captures/{aid}.png).

likelihood.reason: Reachable by the lowest-trust, prompt-injection-assumed agent principal on any desktop-template sandbox using cheap gated calls; only self-limited by serial request rate, not by any code bound.

impact.reason: Persistent unbounded growth of shared host disk under settings.home that is never reclaimed even on sandbox deletion; disk exhaustion degrades the control plane (which also holds docker.sock) and can fail audit writes, which halts further tool calls (AU-2).

confidence.reason: The write site, the absence of any removal (grep-confirmed), and the missing pending cap are all source-visible, and a bounded local harness exercising the real service code shows retained PNGs after deny+expire with no cap.
